# Deposit Cleaning Dispute Checklist for a London Tenancy

Your strongest position is that a landlord can only claim for cleaning if they can show the property was left worse than at move-in, beyond fair wear and tear. Keep everything dated, factual, and tied to the check-in/check-out condition.

## Evidence to Gather and Points to Raise

### Evidence checklist
- Check-in inventory report and any move-in cleaning invoice
- Check-out photos and videos, with timestamps if available
- Move-in and move-out photos of the same rooms/fixtures
- Tenancy agreement clause on wear and tear and cleaning
- Any email/text confirming the flat was professionally cleaned before you moved in
- Receipts for any cleaning you arranged before leaving
- Copies of the landlord’s deduction breakdown and invoices/quotes
- Deposit protection scheme details and any dispute deadline
- A short timeline: tenancy start, tenancy end, checkout date, and handover details

### What to say in the dispute email
- The flat was professionally cleaned before move-in, so the expected standard should be matched against the checkout condition and inventory.
- A claim for “general cleaning” needs evidence of actual additional cleaning required, not a blanket charge.
- Normal wear and tear is allowed under the tenancy agreement, so ordinary use over nearly two years should not be charged as damage or neglect.
- Ask for the specific rooms/items that justify the £680, plus photos, invoices, and the calculation method.
- Point out that dated checkout photos support the condition you left the property in.
- Request that the deduction be reduced or withdrawn unless the landlord can prove a loss beyond fair wear and tear.
- State that you are willing to resolve it promptly through the deposit protection scheme if needed.

### Polite message you can send
Dear [Landlord/Agent Name],

I’m writing about the proposed £680 deduction for “general cleaning” from my deposit for the tenancy at [address], which ended on 28 February 2026.

I would be grateful if you could review this deduction. The flat was professionally cleaned before I moved in, and my tenancy agreement allows for normal wear and tear. I also have dated checkout photos showing the condition I left the property in.

Could you please send:
- the specific areas/items said to require cleaning,
- the photos or other evidence supporting the claim,
- the cleaning invoice or quote,
- and how the £680 figure was calculated.

If the claim is based only on general cleaning rather than a specific loss beyond fair wear and tear, I would ask that it be withdrawn or reduced.

Thank you for reviewing this. I would appreciate a prompt response so we can resolve it amicably.

Kind regards,
[Your Name]

## Quick Actions

- Citizens Advice on tenancy deposits: https://www.citizensadvice.org.uk/housing/renting-a-home/tenancy-deposits/
